newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's KGHM says has not been hedging since 1994.
newsitem.headline: Poland's KGHM says has not been hedging since 1994.

text.p: Poland's KGHM copper concern has not been hedging its copper or silver production since 1994 when it lost 16.7 million zlotys on hedging nine percent of its copper output, the firm said in its issue prospectus on Friday.

"Since that time the company has not been doing hedging transactions for future copper and silver prices so KGHM is now fully exposed to price swings on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and LBM (London bullion market)," the prospectus said.
It said KGHM intended to hedge its production in the future, but such decisions would be made by the board after reviewing the current and forecast situation on the metals market.
"The company sees the positive aspects of strategic hedging and intends to use the mechanism of the derivatives market to manage price risk," the prospectus said.
KGHM, which will start trading on the London and Warsaw bourses on July 10, is the fifth largest copper producer and the largest silver producer in the world.
